questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that the destination was somewhere I have never been before, as well as the location of the university in the given country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy. University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) was really good at sending me all the information I needed for preparing for my stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really recieve any assistance, except for emailing questions to my home- and host university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were both options for an apartment, that you shared with up to three other exchange students (which i chose), but you could also choose to get your own room with your own bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: neither of these were available, but there were lots of restaurants on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: you will both have access to private bathroom (however if you choose the housing with roommates, the bathroom is of course shared between the four of you), and also each housing building on campus has their own laundromat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was relatively quick, i think it took about an hour or so, and the people doing it are very good at keeping the process smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other students were present to answer questions and guiding. There were also signs all over campus to point you in the right direction, and also you were assigned a tutor before arrival, whom you could text if anything popped up.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: keep yourself up to date with the emails they send, and send them an email with your questions if anything is confusing to your - they are very quick at responding.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses weren't that challenging, but they were still interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: in all four of my courses we had two classes a week; one lecture and one seminar. The lectures were much like a lecture at UCPH, but the seminar class was for group working to further elaborate and explain what we had learned at the lecture, but in smaller groups. So for example if there were 100 people in the class, all 100 would attend the lecture, but at the seminar we would be divided into classes of 10-15 people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Studying Literature, Understanding the Chinese Creative Industries, Communication & Technology and Gender & Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all four of my courses since they all provided different and fun experiences. In Studying literatur we had to do a play, and in Communication and Technology we had to do a creative product.

questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food and taxis was way less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: basically all types of sport was available. For cultural activities, we were invited on a trip around the city about twice a month which they called the "Living in China"-tours. I participated in two of these. In one them we went on a tour of a museum, and the other I went rowing in a Dragon boat.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend to go on the universities tours

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: i would strongly encourage people to explore the rest of china in the weekends and holidays. I went to Shanghai multiple times, beijing, shenzhen and much more during my weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it wasnt that difficult, because UNNC is an international university.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: i found it the easiest to find local friends during my classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: learning to use all the apps, that are essential to living in china.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i loved how accesible everything was

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: use your weekends to adventure around China, bring an extra suitcase and pack a lot of summer clothes - it was 35 degrees for the first 1.5 i was there, which i wasnt prepared for.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: use your tutors! they know everything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: making new friends and exploring China.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: juggling exams with the want to adventure. I, and all the other exchange students i talked to, experienced a kinda stressful feeling, because we didn't want to waste our time i China, but also wanted to do well in school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
